name: VCF Operations for Networks 9.1 application onboarding across a token expiry
prompt:
Our platform team runs VCF Operations for Networks 9.1 (the VCF 9.1 successor to vRealize Network Insight) and onboards application definitions exported from the CMDB. Write the PowerShell module that does it.

The repository already has what you need:

- `docs/contract.json` is the wire contract for the four API operations you may use, derived from the VCF Operations for Networks 9.1 OpenAPI specification. `docs/official_sources.json` records exactly where it came from. Treat `docs/contract.json` as authoritative for methods, paths, parameters, property names, enum spellings and the authentication scheme.
- `onboarding/applications.json` is the CMDB export to onboard.
- `mock/` is a loopback stand-in for an appliance. It is pinned to the contract, serves nothing the contract does not name, and records every request it receives.
- `tests/verify.py` is the acceptance test. Run it with `python3 tests/verify.py`; it starts the stand-in for you on an ephemeral loopback port. The acceptance test itself is offline and does not install external packages.

Read `README.md` for the layout.

## What to build

A PowerShell module at `src/VcfOpsNetworksOnboarding/`, with the manifest `VcfOpsNetworksOnboarding.psd1`, exporting exactly one function:

```
Invoke-VcfOpsNetworksApplicationOnboarding
    -Server         <string>         appliance root URL, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8721
    -Credential     <pscredential>
    -DefinitionPath <string>         path to the CMDB export
    [-DomainType    <string>]        LOCAL or LDAP; defaults to LOCAL
    [-DomainValue   <string>]        the domain value, when there is one
    [-PageSize      <int>]           defaults to 100
```

The contract's server base path is `/api/ni`, so a request goes to `<Server>/api/ni<path>`.

It returns an object with:

- `Created` — names of the applications it created, in the order they appear in the export
- `Skipped` — names it left alone because the appliance already had them, in the same order
- `TokenRefreshCount` — how many times it acquired a token *after* the first one

## Session handling

1. Acquire a token with the `create` operation, sending the username, the password and the domain type. That request is not itself authenticated, so it carries no `Authorization` header.
2. Authenticate every other call with the ApiKeyAuth scheme the contract describes.
3. **The appliance can end a session before the expiry it advertised.** Do not refresh pre-emptively and do not poll: acquire a new token only in response to a `401`, then replay the request that was refused, unchanged, and carry on from there. Everything that already succeeded must stay done — nothing may be created twice, and the batch must run to completion.
4. Release the token with the `delete` operation when the run finishes. That is the last request of the run.

## Onboarding

5. Before creating anything, enumerate the applications the appliance already holds, once, using `listApplications`. Ask for `-PageSize` results per page and follow the returned `cursor` until the appliance stops returning one — it caps pages at its own maximum, so expect more than one. Send no query parameters beyond the page size and the cursor.
6. Walk `applications` in file order. If an application of that name already exists, skip it. Otherwise create it with a single `addApplicationWithTiers` call.
7. `If-Match` identifies an existing definition being modified. This run only creates, so it is not sent.

## Mapping the export onto the request body

`AppWithTiersRequest`:

| Body field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` |
| `entity_id` | never sent; the appliance allocates it |
| `source_group_entity_id` | `source_group_entity_id`, when it has entries |
| `enable_intent` | `enable_intent` when it is not null, as a JSON boolean. A null means "leave the appliance default alone" |
| `tiers` | one `TierRequest` per entry of `tiers`, in order |

`TierRequest`:

| Body field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` |
| `entity_id` | never sent; the appliance allocates it |
| `source_group_entity_id` | the export has no such slot for a tier, so never sent |
| `group_membership_criteria` | one entry from `search_membership` and one from `ip_membership`, in that order, for whichever are present; omitted when neither is |
| `member_list` | `vms` from `member_vms`, `physical_ips` from `member_physical_ips`, `kubernetes_services` from `member_kubernetes_services` — each key only when it has entries, and the whole `member_list` omitted when all three are empty |

A search criterion is `{"membership_type": "SearchMembershipCriteria", "search_membership_criteria": {"entity_type": ..., "filter": ...}}` and an IP criterion is `{"membership_type": "IPAddressMembershipCriteria", "ip_address_membership_criteria": {"ip_addresses": [...]}}`. The discriminator values, the property names and the schema names do not all use the same spelling — take each from the contract.

A member is `{"key": {"entity_id": ..., "entity_type": ...}, "name": ...}`. `key` also allows an `entity_name`; the export has nothing to put there, so it is not sent.

## The omission rule

The CMDB export carries a slot for every field whether or not it has a value, and a missing value shows up as `null` or as `[]`. The appliance reads a field that is *present* as an instruction. So:

> Any optional field with no value must be left out of the JSON body entirely. Never send it as `null`, `""`, `[]` or `{}`.

This applies to the credential body as much as to the application bodies — for a LOCAL domain the domain has no value, and the contract says the field is not required for LOCAL.

## Packaging

The module manifest declares `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` in `RequiredModules` as a deployment prerequisite. Do not vendor, bundle or commit any copy of it. The acceptance test checks that declaration but does not download or fake the external package.

## Ground rules

Everything runs against `127.0.0.1`; no live VMware endpoint is involved. Add only `src/`; leave `docs/`, `mock/`, `onboarding/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` and `README.md` as they are.
